bottom_line: In JUPITER, rosuvastatin (20 mg daily) as compared with placebo reduced the rate of the primary end point (hazard ratio, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.46 to 0.69).
implications: In these apparently healthy participants with LDL cholesterol <130 mg/dl and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ≥2.0 mg/liter, the reported data support that rosuvastatin lowered major cardiovascular events versus placebo (primary end point HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.69) and was associated with lower all-cause death (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.67-0.97) over a median 1.9 years of follow-up; however, physician-reported diabetes was more frequent with rosuvastatin (270 vs 216), and the document notes uncertainty about longer-term adverse events given early stopping and short median follow-up.

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in apparently healthy men and women with LDL cholesterol <130 mg/dl and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ≥2.0 mg/liter.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 17,802 apparently healthy men and women with low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels of less than 130 mg per deciliter (3.4 mmol per liter) and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels of 2.0 mg per liter or higher

major_points.text: Primary outcome was a composite of MI, stroke, revascularization, unstable angina hospitalization, or cardiovascular death.
major_points.quote: The primary outcome was the occurrence of a first major cardiovascular event, defined as nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, hospital- ization for unstable angina, an arterial revascu- larization procedure, or confirmed death from cardiovascular causes.

major_points.text: The trial was stopped early after a median follow-up of 1.9 years (maximum 5.0 years).
major_points.quote: The trial was stopped after a median follow-up of 1.9 years (maximum, 5.0).

major_points.text: Rosuvastatin reduced the primary end point rate versus placebo (0.77 vs 1.36 per 100 person-years; HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.46–0.69).
major_points.quote: The rates of the primary end point were 0.77 and 1.36 per 100 per- son-years of follow-up in the rosuvastatin and placebo groups, respectively (hazard ratio for rosuvastatin, 0.56; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.46 to 0.69; P<0.00001)

major_points.text: Death from any cause was lower with rosuvastatin than placebo (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.67-0.97).
Physician-reported diabetes occurred more frequently in the rosuvastatin group than placebo (270 vs 216).
